cohort_rule: All 40 consecutive administrative IDs 700120..700159, FIXED BEFORE opening any of them. No selection by signature count or success. Keep 404/rejected/missing; target of inference restricted to publicly retrievable records in this fixed ID band, not all petitions.
prior_exposure: Past PETITIONS5 includes petition 700143 (one of 40), but no others examined individually in this block. 700143 MUST be marked pre-exposed and excluded in sensitivity.
scope: Empirical UK citizen petition administrative participation, independent of prior UK650 election and last PETITIONS5 top-ranked design
report_asof: 2026-10-28, but source web cache may be older; do not infer current-real-time availability or first_public_at
A: What fraction of a signature-unselected consecutive-ID administrative cohort is recoverable through first-party UK petitions API, with statuses and valid signature count? Does the previous top-12 selection hide denominator missingness?

B.H1: At least 20 distinct API records are publicly accessible of 40 IDs with some below 10k
B.H0: Under 20 or no below-threshold; do not infer near-threshold effect

C: Fetch official .json for all 40 IDs; log HTTP/tool status and original attributes (ID, state, count, created, opened, closed, response and debate event dates). No names/details/political content in derived panel. Never replace unobserved IDs with guessed 0 signatures. Include missingness and prior-exposed 700143.
R1: Intent-to-sample 40 IDs, accessible subset, signed count not person count
R2: Baseline compare top-signed PETITIONS5 coverage only, no policy effect
R3: No random population sample; IDs may be ordered by creation and publication/moderation; missing not at random
R5: If <20 API records or all >10k, stop inferential cycle and switch to source access task
J: Reject pseudo-confirmation from after-event or missing data; R5 governs next action.
